title: Departments where claims costs are rising
question: In which departments did the judgments and claims account grow between fiscal 2019–2022 and fiscal 2023–2026?
finding: The ledger charges $223.8 million to judgments and claims in fiscal 2019 to 2022 and $333.9 million in fiscal 2023 to 2026 (1.49 times as much). 2 departments carried at least half as much again in the later four years, and at least $5 million: Municipal Transportation Agency ($25.6 million to $72.8 million); Public Utilities Commission ($38.7 million to $71.7 million). The account fell most at Public Health ($11.3 million to $1.2 million).
how: The Controller’s Spending and Revenue table, spending lines whose account is “Judgments & Claims”, added up by department for fiscal 2019–2022 and fiscal 2023–2026. Departments with under $1 million over the eight years are left out. “Main line” is the sub-account, as the ledger names it, that holds the most of the department’s total. Sorted by dollars added.
limits: This is where a payment was charged, which is usually the department whose work gave rise to the claim but can be a central account, and money moves between the two from year to year. The account holds legal fees and litigation costs as well as payments to claimants, so a rise can be one long lawsuit rather than more claims. A department that drives buses, polices, runs hospitals or maintains water mains will always carry more. The totals by department for the whole period are in the autopilot file; this screen adds only the direction. What would settle it: the City Attorney’s claims report by department, with counts of claims filed, paid and denied.
